title: Control plane API for Dedicated rollout plans (CRUD + promote/abort + audit hooks)
creator: Ethan Park
project: Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools
description:
Goal
Implement the control-plane API surface and persistence for Dedicated staged rollout plans, including deterministic promote/abort actions, validation rules, and audit-event emission hooks.

This ticket is the control-plane foundation for “Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools”. It should unblock Console workflow (ENG-5980) and policy/routing integration (ENG-5941 / ENG-5950) by providing a stable resource model and action semantics.

Background / context
Dedicated customers require safer upgrades for reserved pools (model versions, runtime builds, routing policies, config). We need an auditable, reversible, stage-by-stage rollout plan attached to a Dedicated pool, with explicit promotion and abort semantics.

Scope (in)
1) Persistence schema
- Add data model + DB migrations for DedicatedPoolRolloutPlan, including:
  - pool_id (and account_id / org_id for RBAC scoping)
  - rollout target (e.g., model_version_id, runtime_build_id, routing_policy_id, config_hash)
  - stages (ordered; traffic % or replica partitions as per ADR)
  - state machine fields (draft/running/held/aborted/completed) and current_stage_index
  - gate configuration references (v1: Redwood-defined gates; v2: more flexible)
  - timestamps: created_at, updated_at, started_at, completed_at, aborted_at
  - concurrency / idempotency: version (optimistic lock), last_action_idempotency_key
- Backfill strategy for existing pools is out-of-scope for this ticket but migrations must be compatible with ENG-6011.

2) CRUD APIs
- Endpoints (names are illustrative; align with existing control-plane conventions):
  - POST /v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollout-plans
  - GET /v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollout-plans/{plan_id}
  - GET /v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollout-plans (list; filter by status)
  - PATCH /v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollout-plans/{plan_id} (mutable fields: display_name, description, stage definitions in draft, gate config, scheduling hints)
- Validation rules at create/update time:
  - Stage monotonicity (e.g., 0% < 1% < 10% < 50% < 100% OR increasing replica partitions)
  - Exactly one terminal “100%” stage (or “all replicas”) unless explicitly configured; defaults from Product thread are 1/10/50/100.
  - Minimum pool size and minimum headroom rules must be enforced (initially: hard guardrails + warnings) using values from infra guidelines.
  - Disallow edits to stage definitions once running (except admin-only “hold” notes); mutable fields should be explicit.
  - Validate multi-region constraints (cannot define stage partition that would strand a region below min replicas).
  - Ensure rollout target is “pinnable” and compatible with pool’s model family / hardware profile (basic validation only; deep compatibility in routing/data plane).

3) Promote / abort actions
- Endpoints:
  - POST /v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollout-plans/{plan_id}:promote
  - POST /v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollout-plans/{plan_id}:abort
- Semantics:
  - Promote increments current_stage_index by exactly 1; promotion is rejected if plan is not in running state.
  - Abort transitions to aborted state and resets active routing target to baseline (baseline reference stored on plan start).
  - Idempotency keys required for promote/abort to avoid double-promote on retries.
  - Optimistic concurrency required (If-Match / plan version) to avoid races between Console and automation.
  - Manual override actions (force-promote/hold) are explicitly out-of-scope here; those are tracked separately and must be admin-guarded.

4) Audit hooks
- Emit audit events for:
  - rollout_plan.created
  - rollout_plan.updated
  - rollout_plan.started (if “start” becomes distinct; if not, capture first promote from draft->running)
  - rollout_plan.promoted (include from_stage, to_stage, gates summary pointer)
  - rollout_plan.aborted
- Event payload fields must satisfy security/compliance spec:
  - actor (user/service), actor_type, account_id/org_id, pool_id, plan_id
  - request_id, idempotency_key
  - reason/comment (required for abort; optional for promote)
  - old_state/new_state, old_stage/new_stage
- Ensure export pipeline compatibility is tracked (INT-1951 is separate, but we should coordinate event type names now).

Out of scope (explicit)
- Gate evaluation engine implementation (ENG-5941)
- Data-plane routing behavior (ENG-5950)
- Console UI / customer-facing workflows (ENG-5980 / DES-431)
- Full experiment platform / arbitrary customer-defined metrics

Acceptance criteria
- DB migrations ship cleanly and are reversible.
- CRUD endpoints support create/get/list/patch with RBAC enforcement by account + pool.
- Promote/abort endpoints are idempotent and concurrency-safe.
- Validation blocks obviously unsafe stage plans (non-monotonic, missing terminal stage, violates min partition sizing constraints).
- All mutating actions emit audit events with required fields.
- Unit tests cover validation rules + state machine transitions; integration test stubs exist (full E2E in ENG-5995).

Implementation notes / decisions
- Resource shape: plan is a first-class resource under pool, not embedded directly into pool config (per platform API-shape thread). This avoids large pool config diffs and allows independent auditing.
- State machine (v1): draft -> running -> (held) -> completed OR aborted. “held” will be used by later ticket if needed; for this ticket we store state but do not build automation.
- Missing-metrics behavior is not decided here; gate evaluation will handle (likely fail-closed with admin override).

- Design spec: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/staged-rollouts-for-dedicated-pools-design-spec.json
- ADRs:
  - Stage model: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-dedicated-rollout-stage-model.json
  - Gate signals: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-gate-evaluation-signals-and-thresholds.json
  - Rollback semantics: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-rollback-and-abort-semantics-for-dedicated-rollouts.json
- GitHub PRs:
  - PR #28411 add rollout plan model + migrations
  - PR #28437 CRUD + validation
  - PR #28458 promote/abort + audit events + idempotency

Test plan
- Unit tests:
  - stage validation (monotonicity, terminal stage, min partition)
  - state transition guards for promote/abort
  - idempotency: same key returns same result (no double increment)
  - optimistic concurrency: stale version rejected
- Integration (light): create plan -> promote -> abort -> verify audit events emitted (mock sink).

Rollout / deployment notes
- Must be behind feature flag for beta enablement (ENG-6011). API endpoints may exist but return 404/feature-disabled for non-enabled accounts.
- Migration timing needs coordination with release train (see eng-releases thread); avoid long locks.

Risks
- Validation too strict for small pools: ensure infra guardrails have escape hatch (admin override) but keep v1 safe. Capture “warning vs error” decisions in code comments.
- Audit event schema churn: align with Security (Kaitlyn) before merging.

comments: 2025-02-04 (Ethan Park): Kicking off ENG-5932. Please align API resource shape with the eng-platform thread (plan as first-class resource under pool). Also make sure we have idempotency + optimistic concurrency from day 1—Console will retry aggressively.

2025-02-06 (Benji Okafor): Drafted schema + migrations (PR #28411). Includes plan.state, current_stage_index, stages_jsonb, and baseline_target snapshot. Question: do we treat first promote as “start” transition from draft->running, or add an explicit start endpoint?

2025-02-07 (Jordan Lee): Prefer implicit start on first promote; keeps action surface smaller. Policy engine will key off plan.state == running and stage_index >= 0. Ensure audit event captures draft->running transition.

2025-02-10 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): Audit events must include actor_type (human vs service), request_id, and idempotency_key. Also: abort reason should be required (string) for compliance workflows. Please ensure RBAC checks use account_id + pool_id scoping, not just pool_id.

2025-02-12 (Benji Okafor): CRUD endpoints up in PR #28437. Validation: monotonic stages, requires terminal 100%, blocks edits to stages once running. Added conservative min partition check (>= 1 replica equivalent) with a TODO to hook into infra sizing table.

2025-02-14 (Irene Choi): Infra note: for small pools we should not allow 1% stage if it maps to <1 GPU. Validation should be based on effective replica count per region, not just percentage. If we can’t compute reliably in control plane yet, default to blocking percentage stages for pools < N GPUs unless stage uses explicit replica partitions.

2025-02-18 (Benji Okafor): Added “stage_strategy” field (percentage vs replicas) and validation that percentage strategy requires pool_size >= 16 GPUs (configurable constant for now). Replica strategy allowed for smaller pools. Will follow up with Vanessa for exact thresholds; leaving a config knob for SRE to tune.

2025-02-21 (Benji Okafor): Promote/abort endpoints implemented in PR #28458. Promote increments stage index; abort sets aborted and stores aborted_at. Both accept Idempotency-Key header; stored last_key + last_result hash. Added If-Match support for plan version.

2025-02-24 (Rafael Mendes): Please ensure abort immediately disables stage routing target in control plane output. Even if data plane is eventually consistent, we need the control plane to publish baseline_target for routers to pick up quickly.
2025-02-25 (Benji Okafor): Confirmed: abort response includes baseline_target and plan state changes; routers will poll and converge. Added audit event rollout_plan.aborted with reason required.

2025-02-27 (Ethan Park): Reviewed PR #28458. LGTM with one ask: make promote idempotency robust across deploys (avoid in-memory). Looks like you persisted key in DB—good. Also ensure list endpoint supports filtering by status for Console.

2025-03-03 (Benji Okafor): All three PRs merged (#28411, #28437, #28458). Added release note in control-plane changelog and confirmed feature-flag gate returns feature-disabled for non-enabled accounts. Handing off to Console team for endpoint wiring (ENG-5980).

2025-03-04 (Chloe Martin): Confirmed endpoints + response schema work for timeline rendering. We’ll start integrating once gate evidence endpoint lands (ENG-5980). Minor request: include stage display_name in GET payload (we can compute, but better server-side). Filed follow-up ENG-6039.
